text:
Alice K: Quick heads-up — new user hit onboarding snag after doing an API key rotation. Their sampleapp started sending requests under a different org/project than they expected. Anyone seen this before?
Sam V: ugh, that sounds familiar. Do you have the exact env+cli steps they used?
Alice K: Repro steps from user pasted below. they rotated key via console, then ran `./sampleapp --project onboarding-demo`. App ended up in `org=acme, project=default` instead of their org.
Alice K: Env at runtime (redacted):
```
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk-live-REDACTED"
export REDWOOD_ORG="user-org"
export REDWOOD_PROJECT="onboarding-demo"
# they also had local ~/.redwood/config with a saved project
```
Ben C: Hmm. Could be env-var precedence vs key-scoped metadata. The new key might be scoped to a different org/project and our SDK currently prefers key metadata over explicit env vars in some language bindings.
Maria L: That would explain it — if the runtime reads key metadata first and overrides env vars, rotation would switch the app scope without user noticing. :thinking_face:
Sam V: Which SDK was this? Node or Python? We have historically had parity gaps where node used CLI flags > env > key, and python did key > env.
Alice K: User was on the node sampleapp. I would've expected CLI flag to win. They passed `--project` too.
Ben C: Ok that suggests a bug: node SDK should respect explicit CLI flags/project args highest. If key-scoped metadata is trumping them that's wrong.
Maria L: Can someone create a tiny repro? I can add a quick integration test to catch this. Also we should update sampleapp docs to call out rotation caveat until fixed.
Sam V: I'll try to reproduce locally — quick checklist: spin up sampleapp, create two API keys scoped to different orgs, rotate env var, run with `--project` and watch effective scope in logs.
Alice K: Logs showed this warning: `warn: API key scope (org: acme, project: default) differs from requested scope (user-org/onboarding-demo) — using key scope` — so code path is explicitly preferring key.
Ben C: I'll open an issue and mark as P1 for parity bug. If it's node-only we still need both SDKs aligned.
cred-rotation-bot: Issue #412 created: "sdk-auth-env-precedence-rotation-quirk" assigned to @Ben C — https://tracker.redwood/412
Maria L: Filing a docs PR too. I'll add a short note under "Key rotation" and link to the issue.
Ben C: Action: I'll add unit test + patch in node SDK to prefer CLI > env > key metadata, and add an integration check.
Sam V: If anyone wants to pair on the repro I can be available in 30.
Alice K: Thanks y'all — I'll follow up with user once there's a fix. :thumbsup:
